diagram: diagram: { width, height, style: "sketch"|"clean", background?, name?, elements: [...] }. Elements: rect | ellipse | diamond | text (x, y, w, h, label, fill?, stroke?, fontSize?), and arrow | line (from/to = ids of shapes, label?, dashed?, or points: [[x,y],...]). Give shapes ids to connect them. Leave room for arrow labels (at least ~140px between shapes). Outputs <name>.svg, <name>.png (2x) and <name>.excalidraw (editable in Excalidraw).
html-still: html-still: { files: [{name, content}|{name, url}], entry: "index.html", viewports: [{width, height, scale?}], fullPage?, name? }. Write self-contained HTML/CSS. Renders have no internet: put assets in files, or use https://studio.local/lib/gsap/gsap.min.js, https://studio.local/lib/three/build/three.module.js (import map "three" and "three/addons/" → https://studio.local/lib/three/examples/jsm/), https://studio.local/lib/rough/rough.esm.js. One PNG per viewport.
design-review: design-review: { files + entry, or url: "https://…" (a public page), widths?: [375, 768, 1440] }. Outputs a full-page screenshot per width and findings.json (sideways scroll, contrast, tap targets, small text, images, headings, meta). Look at the screenshots yourself too: the checks don't judge layout, hierarchy or taste.
ffmpeg: ffmpeg: { files: [{name, url}], args: [...] }. Arguments only, no shell; name files as {in:clip.mp4} and outputs as {out:final.mp4}. No paths, URLs, or filters that read files (movie, textfile, fontfile, subtitles); drawtext with text= and font= is fine. Probe with a short render first if unsure. Prefer -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart for MP4.
html-video: html-video: { files, entry, width, height, fps (≤60), seconds, audio?: file name, name?: "video.mp4" }. Frame-accurate: the page runs on virtual time (requestAnimationFrame, performance.now, Date.now). GSAP timelines, CSS animations and three.js loops render exactly; for anything else define window.seek = (t) => {...} to draw the frame at t seconds. Don't rely on setTimeout. Load GSAP/three from https://studio.local/lib/ (no internet).
manim: manim: { files: [{name: "scene.py", content}], entry: "scene.py", scene: "ClassName", quality: "l"|"m"|"h"|"k" }. Standard Manim Community; no internet. Output <Scene>.mp4.
reel: reel: { files, entry: "index.html", name?: "film.mp4", from?, to? }. A Reel film: in the page, import { film, clip, series, tween, ease, spring, keys, stagger, split, typewriter, fade, slide, wipe, zoom, blur, image, video } from "/_reel/reel.js"; const f = film({ width, height, fps }); f.add(clip({ at, for, enter: fade(0.4), setup: (root) => {...build elements, return state}, draw: (state, { t, progress }) => {...set everything from t} })); f.audio("music.mp3", { at, volume, fadeIn, fadeOut }); f.captions([{ at, for, text }]); f.mount(). draw must depend only on t. Video layers (video("clip.mp4", { at, for, trim, film: f })) are frame-exact and their sound is mixed in. Outputs the MP4 plus .srt and .vtt captions. Size and length come from the film and must fit your tier.
blender: blender: { files: [{name: "scene.py", content}], entry }. Headless Blender (bpy), factory settings. Write outputs into the directory given after "--" (sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1]): .glb via bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=..., export_format="GLB"), renders via bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True). Resolution limits are in env ORVYN_MAX_WIDTH/ORVYN_MAX_HEIGHT.
ai-video: ai-video: { prompt, seconds, width, height, seed? }. Generates clips on a GPU worker. Never depict a real person's likeness or voice.
world-3d: world-3d: { model: "lyra" | "hunyuanworld", image: file name (the picture to build from), prompt?, seed?, options?, files }. An explorable 3D scene: lyra writes Gaussian splats (.ply); hunyuanworld writes a 360° panorama and a layered mesh. Use a sharp, well-lit image with clear depth. Some models' licences don't cover every country: if one is refused for this client, use the other.
world-video: world-video: { model: "yume" | "worldplay" | "gamecraft", image: file name (where the walk starts), prompt? (the world), actions: [{ keys: "w" | "w+right" | "none"…, seconds, caption? }], width?, height?, fps?, files }. A video walking through the world: w a s d move, up down left right look, space jumps, "none" stands still. Keep steps short (1–4 s) and the whole path within your tier's video length. If a model is refused for this client's country, use yume.
long-video: long-video: { model: "helios" | "longlive", segments: [{ prompt, seconds }], image?: file name, width?, height?, fps? }. One long video that follows a timeline of prompts: each segment's prompt steers that stretch, so describe how the scene changes rather than starting over. Never depict a real person's likeness or voice.
